3. It is argued that the complainant belongs to Mangathar within the jurisdiction of Pali District Umaria, therefore, the matter was sent to Pali through P.S. Umaria on which an FIR at Crime No.103/2018 was registered.

It is submitted that a written complaint was made by the respondent No.2 - Saira Bano pointing out the fact she got married to Rahat Khan on 05.10.2015 and after one month of the marriage, her husband, father-in-law, mother-in-law and sister-in-law demanded dowry and caused harassment to her mentally and physically.
It was further alleged that her sister-in-law was involved in flesh trading and her husband and in-laws used to force her in flesh trading which she refused.

A threatening was given by her husband to give divorce and an amount of Rs.2,00,000/-
was demanded as dowry from her.
When she got pregnant, her husband and her in-laws did not want the child and she was given medicines to abort the child by her husband and in- laws.
When she was pregnant on second occasion, she has not given any information regarding her pregnancy to her husband and in-laws.
Thereafter she was sent to her parental house.

On 03.03.2018, the complainant and her NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:45042 3 MCRC-23593-2018 family went to her in-laws house along with Anjuman Committee for compromise but the complainant's in-laws refused to keep her in their house.
Therefore, the FIR was got registered.

After completion of investigation by the police authorities, the charge sheet was filed by the police station Pali before the Judicial Magistrate First Class, Birsinghpur Pali, District Umaria on which cognizance was taken on 02.05.2018.

sentences.text:
When the factum of registration of criminal case came into knowledge of the petitioner - Shama, she has filed an application to the various authorities i.e.
Superintendent of Police, District Umaria, Inspector General of Police, Shahdol informing the fact that she is already married and has been settled in Bilaspur for the past thirteen years.
She is having a son aged about 10 years.
He is living separately approximately 250 Kms away, thus there is no question regarding demand of dowry by the sister-in-law.
Her husband owns a house at Bilaspur since 2009 and before that they used to live in a rented house.

Several documents are being filed to substantiate the said argument that the petitioners are residing at Bilaspur i.e. the birth certificate of her son issued in the year 2007 from Budhiya Hospital and Maternity Home Bilaspur.
Caste certificate issued from Nagar Palika Nigam Bilaspur.
Son studying in DAV Public School, Bilaspur etc.
It is argued that they are having no connection with the so said offences registered against her.

Attention of this Court is drawn to the statement of Fatima Begum i.e. mother of the complainant recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. to the effect that on 07.02.2018 the husband and family members did not permit the complainant to enter the house.

It is argued that at the relevant time,
the petitioner was at Bilaspur.

sentences.text: She being the sister-in- law residing at Bilaspur separately, no case for offence punishable under Sections 498-A, 323, 34 of Indian Penal Code and also under Section 3, 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act is made out against the petitioner.
He has drawn attention of this Court to the FIR registered against her on 17.03.2018 wherein there are only general and omnibus allegation has been made against her.
4. As far as petitioner - Shabnam Khan is concerned, it is argued that the petitioner is innocent and she has not committed any offence in any manner.
She is residing at Umaria since last 10 years.
No prima facie case is made out against the petitioner - Shabnam.
It is submitted that the respondent No.2 lodged a report at police station after receiving the notice of divorce.
The complainant was residing separately in her parental house and, therefore, the petitioner - Shabnam has no connection with the alleged offence.
There is no specific allegation against the petitioner.
Only general and omnibus allegations have been levelled against the petitioner.
She has been falsely implicated in the matter.
On these grounds, they have prayed for quashment of FIR and all consequential proceedings.
4. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the respondents/State has vehemently opposed the contentions.
It is argued that the allegations levelled with respect to demand of dowry are not general.

The record even indicates NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:45042 5 MCRC-23593-2018 that the complainant and the family members along with the member of the Committee went to the house of the petitioners to get the matter compromised between the parties but the same was not compromised.
There are specific allegations of harassment and demand of dowry and also for giving medicines to the complainant to get her pregnancy aborted.
Despite attempts being made by her/complainant to settle the issue, the husband and in-laws have not permitted her to enter the matrimonial house.
It is argued that the interference in such matters should be very limited as there are specific allegations against the petitioners.
The same being a matter of evidence could not have been dealt with by this Court for quashment of a criminal proceedings.

It is also submitted that interference in the cases of quashment of the FIR can be made in a very rare cases as has been considered and held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of State of Haryana Vs. Bhajanlal reported in 1992 Suppl. SCC 335 .

The complaint was made to the Inspector General.

7. This petition has been filed on the ground that the petitioners being the sister-in-law are residing separately in Bilaspur at Chhattisgarh and Umaria.

The petitioner - Shama @ Shristi Singh has also filed an application to the senior police authorities on 28.04.2018 regarding her false implication in the case but no action has been taken by the authorities.

Several documents have been filed to substantiate their arguments that both the petitioners are residing separately at Bilaspur,
Chhattisgarh and Umaria.
The fact of false implication in such criminal cases was taken note off by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in large number of cases.

8. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Geeta Mehrotra vs State of U.P. reported in (2012) 10 SCC 741 , it is observed as under :
"21.

sentences.text: It would be relevant at this stage to take note of an apt observation of this Court recorded in the matter of G.V. Rao vs. L.H.V. Prasad & Ors. reported in (2000) 3 SCC 693 wherein also in a matrimonial dispute, this Court had held that the High Court should have quashed the complaint arising out of a matrimonial dispute wherein all family members had been roped into the matrimonial litigation which was quashed and set aside.

entities.text: G.V. Rao vs. L.H.V. Prasad & Ors. reported in (2000) 3 SCC 693
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Their Lordships observed therein with which we entirely agree that:
"there has been an outburst of matrimonial dispute in NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-JBP:45042 7 MCRC-23593-2018 recent times.
Marriage is a sacred ceremony, main purpose of which is to enable the young couple to settle down in life and live peacefully.

But little matrimonial skirmishes suddenly erupt which often assume serious proportions resulting in heinous crimes in which elders of the family are also involved with the result that those who could have counselled and brought about rapprochement are rendered helpless on their being arrayed as accused in the criminal case.

There are many reasons which need not be mentioned here for not encouraging matrimonial litigation so that the parties may ponder over their defaults and terminate the disputes amicably by mutual agreement instead of fighting it out in a court of law where it takes years and years to conclude and in that process the parties lose their "young" days in chasing their cases in different courts."

The view taken by the judges in this matter was that the courts would not encourage such disputes."
9 .
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam vs State of Bihar reported in (2022) 6 SCC 599 has held as under - "10.

sentences.text: Having perused the relevant facts and contentions made by the Appellants and Respondents, in our considered opinion, the foremost issue which requires determination in the instant case is whether allegations made against the in-laws Appellants are in the nature of general omnibus allegations and therefore liable to be quashed?

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Before we delve into greater detail on the nature and content of allegations made, it becomes pertinent to mention that incorporation of section 498A of IPC was aimed at preventing cruelty committed upon a woman by her husband and her in-laws, by facilitating rapid state intervention.

However, it is equally true, that in recent times, matrimonial litigation in the country has also increased significantly and there is a greater disaffection and friction surrounding the institution of marriage, now, more than ever.
This has resulted in an increased tendency to employ provisions such as 498A IPC as instruments to settle personal scores against the husband and his relatives.

The abovementioned decisions clearly demonstrate that this Court has at numerous instances expressed concern over the misuse of Section 498- AIPC and the increased tendency of implicating relatives of the husband in matrimonial disputes, without analysing the long-term ramifications of a trial on the complainant as well as the accused.

It is further manifest from the said judgments that false implication by way of general omnibus allegations made in the course of matrimonial dispute,
if left unchecked would result in misuse of the process of law.

Therefore, this Court by way of its judgments has warned the courts from proceeding against the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-JBP:45042 8 MCRC-23593-2018 relatives and in-laws of the husband when no prima facie case is made out against them.
18. Coming to the facts of this case, upon a perusal of the contents of the FIR dated 01.04.19, it is revealed that general allegations are levelled against the Appellants.
The complainant alleged that 'all accused harassed her mentally and threatened her of terminating her pregnancy'.

Furthermore,
no specific and distinct allegations have been made against either of the Appellants herein, i.e., none of the Appellants have been attributed any specific role in furtherance of the general allegations made against them.
This simply leads to a situation wherein one fails to ascertain the role played by each accused in furtherance of the offence.
The allegations are therefore general and omnibus and can at best be said to have been made out on account of small skirmishes.
Insofar as husband is concerned, since he has not appealed against the order of the High court, we have not examined the veracity of allegations made against him.
However, as far as the Appellants are concerned, the allegations made against them being general and omnibus, do not warrant prosecution. ...

21. Therefore, upon consideration of the relevant circumstances and in the absence of any specific role attributed to the appellant-accused, it would be unjust if the appellants are forced to go through the tribulations of a trial i.e. general and omnibus allegations cannot manifest in a situation where the relatives of the complainant's husband are forced to undergo trial.

It has been highlighted by this Court in varied instances, that a criminal trial leading to an eventual acquittal also inflicts severe scars upon the accused, and such an exercise must, therefore, be discouraged."
10.
The complete charge sheet has been placed on record to show that only general and omnibus allegation has been made against the petitioners.
The tendency of implicating each and every family member in matrimonial cases could not be ruled out.
As there are no specific allegation against the petitioners, this Court deems it appropriate to quash the proceedings as far as the present petitioners are concerned.
